answer: A practical sybil defense is bonded grafting. A new agent may join only by being spliced onto a reputation vine, where each established attestor locks slashable stake against that identity for several epochs. Attestors are randomly drawn from a wide ocean of uncorrelated clusters, so a workshop cannot farm its own neighbors. If later behavior matches a clone swarm, those bonds are burned; if the identity stays distinct, the stake is returned as a velvet lining rather than a prize, merely restoring what was risked.
